It is also alleged that the defendant No. 3 had given an undertaking on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in order to settle the dispute and on that undertaking clearance was given to MV Hios to go out from the territorial water of Bangladesh. Ultimately the defendant No. 3 had retracted from its undertaking and repudiated any liability whatsoever for the alleged damage to the injured vessel. The vessel was repaired in Khulna Dockyard and as per terms of Insurance Policy the proforma defendant No Alodged claim to the Insurer namely, the present plaintiff. After considering the papers and documents the plaintiff paid a sum of Tk. 6,27,039.86 for the repairing costs and compensation of the injured vessel. Thereafter the plaintiff namely, the issurer filed this present suit for a decree of the aforesaid amount together with compensation at the rate of 12% per annum till realisation of decretal amount against the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3. 

 17. It has been found above that both MV Zahirabad and MV Hios were equally responsible for their negligence and for such negligence of both the ships such an accident took place. It is also found that if the ratio of responsibility cannot be determined then both the parties will be equally liable for the damage. On this Mr. Rahim submits that then a decree for half of the claim made by the plaintiff should be passed against the defendant Nos.1 and 2 and such a decree can be executed according to law in the foreign country. Submission of Mr. Rahim apparently is very reasonable but the fact remains that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were personally liable for the damage caused to the coaster MV Zahirabad, but they were not properly made parties in the suit. They were not given notice to their address in the foreign country. In the absence of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 a decree by this Court cannot be passed. Had the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 authorised the defendant No. 3 to contest the suit on their behalf by a specific letter or authority, then this question might have been considered. It is found that the defendant No. 3 is not in any way responsible for the alleged damage caused by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 unless and until the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are legally and properly notified and brought on records in the proceeding, a decree against them (foreigners) cannot be passed and as such the submission of Mr. Rahim has no substance.
